newsitem.title: USA: TENPIN BOWLING-OFFICIALS HOLD OFF ON NEW RECORD RULING.
newsitem.headline: TENPIN BOWLING-OFFICIALS HOLD OFF ON NEW RECORD RULING.

text.p: The American Bowling Congress (ABC) said Monday that it had not yet been able to rule that a student at the University of Nebraska set a record when he bowled three consecutive 300 games Sunday.
Spectators at Sun Valley Lanes in Lincoln, Nebraska, said Jeremy Sonnenfeld rolled a 900 series, or three perfect games in a row.

Jack Mordini, an ABC spokesman, said his organisation would like to make a ruling as soon as possible but had not yet received the necessary paperwork from Sonnenfeld. Mordini said the ABC should issue a ruling later in the week.
In order to roll a 300 game, a bowler must hit 12 consecutive strikes. Sonnenfeld rolled 36 strikes in a row, something that has never happened in the ABC's 101-year history.

"I don't know if there is a comparable sporting achievement, but I think it would be like getting a hole in one on every par three in a round of golf," Mordini told Reuters. "It's absolute perfection in a three-game series."
Mordini said Sonnenfeld, 20, was being heralded as "the Tiger Woods of bowling" because of his dedication to the sport.

Mordini said there have been at least four 900 series reported but none officially recognised by the ABC for various reasons, including unsanctioned tournaments and lane conditions that failed to meet ABC standards.
